persona: Everyday customer: traveller, trekker, diver, kitesurfer, wildlife lover

designs.title: Summit Ridge
designs.why: The roped team on the ridge is the bit I'd actually buy, but from 3 m the print breaks into two floating clusters of broken strokes. The summit outline is dashed and full of gaps, and '6,861 m' points at a peak with no name, so it means nothing to me.
designs.fix: Name the peak, or drop the height, and join the upper range to the climbers' ridge in one solid mass so it reads as a single mountain.

designs.title: Kitesurfing
designs.why: The pose is right: rider sitting back against the pull, spray coming off the rail, kite well up on long lines. It looks great on black and I'd wear it to the beach. A lot of the middle is just empty lines, though, and the KITESURFING word is tiny.
designs.fix: Make the KITESURFING caption bigger and bolder so it holds up at the same scale as the rider.

designs.title: Coral
designs.why: A natural history plate that feels like a museum print. The branching texture is rich and holds up up close, and the corallite views reward a diver who looks closer. Works on both tees.
designs.fix: Name the species under CORAL. (for example Acropora) to make it feel like a real plate and less like generic coral.

designs.title: Antarctica
designs.why: Clean, readable family group with a chick that gets an 'aww'. It's a memory piece for anyone who has done the expedition cruise. The penguins lean a bit cartoony, and the heavy sans-serif heading doesn't match the engraved drawing.
designs.fix: Set ANTARCTICA in the same serif style as the other plates and add a little ice or ground shading so the group isn't floating.

designs.title: Bait Ball
designs.why: The one people would ask me about. It reads instantly as a bait ball from across a dive shop, the spiral has real movement, and the scattered fish at the edge are drawn properly. Best on black.
designs.fix: Add a hint of a predator (a sailfish or a diver's silhouette) cutting the edge of the ball to give it a story; otherwise leave it.

designs.title: Beluga
designs.why: The pose is nice, but the body is a huge blank outline with stipple only along a few edges, so on the tee it looks unfinished, like a colouring-book whale. The caption type is muddy and heavy.
designs.fix: Stipple the body's volume (head melon, belly shadow, flipper) so the whale has form, and clean up the caption type.

designs.title: Humpback Whale
designs.why: I love the subject and the body engraving is excellent, but as a shirt it's a textbook page. The labels are too small to read on the body, the leader ticks float without touching anything, and 'Fluke (ventral view)' is wrong on a side-view whale.
designs.fix: Cut most of the labels (keep the body, maybe the baleen) or connect every leader line properly and fix the wrong annotations.

designs.title: Octopus
designs.why: Bold, balanced, full of texture, with curling arms that read from across the street. The Latin name is a nice touch for divers. Instantly wearable.
designs.fix: Offer it on black too; it looks even better there.

designs.title: Patagonia
designs.why: Having trekked there, Fitz Roy, Torre and San Lorenzo with real heights make me smile. But the line work is thin and the bottom half is filler hills, and the name labels are far too small to read on a worn shirt.
designs.fix: Make the peak labels bigger, add some shading weight to the Fitz Roy massif, and crop the empty foothills.

designs.title: El Calafate
designs.why: The distances look believable and the hand-drawn signpost is well made, but it reads like an airport souvenir shirt: lots of text and little feeling. I'd buy Ushuaia or Patagonia before this.
designs.fix: Put a small Perito Moreno glacier or Fitz Roy skyline behind the post to give it a sense of place, and cut it to five arms.

designs.title: Ushuaia
designs.why: Dense and beautifully engraved: peaks, town and reflections. It reads like a real place from 3 m, and the caption and coordinates are crisp and correct. The end-of-the-world shirt I'd want after the trip.
designs.fix: Offer it on black as well; the snow peaks pop there.

designs.title: Belize
designs.why: The palm caye and jetty are lovely, but the reef chart below is a sparse, unlabelled blob with a few random soundings, so the two halves feel stitched together. The coordinates land on the Great Blue Hole, which a diver would love, but nothing tells you so.
designs.fix: Make the chart clearly the Blue Hole and Lighthouse Reef (draw the circular hole, add a small 'Great Blue Hole' label) so the lower half earns its space.
